I am a postdoctoral researcher at CREST (ENSAE Paris, Institut Polytechnique de Paris),
working with Arnak Dalalyan. My research has two strands. The first is the mathematics of
generative models: how diffusion and flow matching models behave in the small-noise
regime, and how their samplers propagate errors. The second is human–AI collaboration in
mathematical research. I designed and built
[Human–AI Mathematics](https://human-ai-mathematics.github.io/), an open framework in
which AI agents search for and cross-review proofs, and every claim they certify can be
checked by a mathematician.

I came to this from both research and industry. After a PhD in statistics at
École Polytechnique on Langevin sampling, and an internship at Google Brain, I spent six
years building machine learning systems: signal processing, object detection and anomaly
detection at Thales, deep learning for drug discovery at Iktos, then foundation models
for biology at MBZUAI and GenBio AI. In 2025 I worked closer to end users, building
proofs of concept for AI decision-support tools and freelancing on LLM systems, from
evaluating LLM answers at Rollstack to improving retrieval at Clarifeye.

What ties it together is taking an idea from paper to working system, and measuring
whether it actually works. Publications are on the [Research](research.qmd) page, code
on [Projects](projects.qmd), and longer notes on the [blog](blog.qmd). To get in touch,
[send me an email]{#contact-email}.

[My postdoctoral work is funded by the European Research Council (ERC) under the European
Union's Horizon Europe research and innovation programme (grant agreement
No. 101201229).]{.small .text-muted}
